evidence.claim: The official biography identifies Abdel Fattah El-Sisi as Egypt's eighth president and lists his prior command roles, including commander-in-chief and minister of defense.
evidence.title: President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi
evidence.publisher: Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The official biography identifies Abdel Fattah El-Sisi as Egypt's eighth president and lists his prior command roles, including commander-in-chief and minister of defense.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary state biography for the incumbent ruler; stable office-identity evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to El-Sisi's office and prior military authority; not a claim about nuclear conduct.
contrary_evidence: Biography is self-authored state material and does not by itself prove how he used authority in 2022.

evidence.claim: Amnesty says Egyptian authorities responded to leaked prison-abuse videos by investigating detainees and their associates instead of the police officers implicated, and that the videos show detainees with injuries and stress-position abuse.
evidence.title: Egypt: Investigate police officers, not detainees, for leaked torture videos
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty says Egyptian authorities responded to leaked prison-abuse videos by investigating detainees and their associates instead of the police officers implicated, and that the videos show detainees with injuries and stress-position abuse.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights investigation with direct review of the videos and follow-on state response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Under Sisi's security apparatus and prosecution system; the report concerns state handling, not a private actor.
contrary_evidence: The Ministry of Interior denied the videos were authentic and claimed the detainees self-harmed.

evidence.claim: Amnesty and HRW say Egyptian authorities failed to conduct an independent, effective, transparent investigation into economist Ayman Hadhoud's custodial death and ignored evidence of enforced disappearance, torture, and ill-treatment.
evidence.title: Egypt: Flawed investigation into death in custody missed opportunity for justice
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty and HRW say Egyptian authorities failed to conduct an independent, effective, transparent investigation into economist Ayman Hadhoud's custodial death and ignored evidence of enforced disappearance, torture, and ill-treatment.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph and body paragraphs on investigation failures
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Joint rights investigation with direct sourcing from official records, witness interviews, and forensic review.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to state security, prosecution, and detention authorities operating under Sisi.
contrary_evidence: Officials said the death was non-criminal and attributed it to cardiac causes.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch reported that Egyptian authorities detained hundreds of people nationwide, and that ECRF documented nearly 700 detentions across 18 governorates between October 1 and November 14, 2022, after social-media calls for anti-government protests.
evidence.title: Egypt: Detentions, Repression Follow Protest Calls
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch reported that Egyptian authorities detained hundreds of people nationwide, and that ECRF documented nearly 700 detentions across 18 governorates between October 1 and November 14, 2022, after social-media calls for anti-government protests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous independent monitoring with detailed detention counts from a local rights group.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi state and its security services; the arrests were made by Egyptian authorities.
contrary_evidence: Authorities framed the arrests as lawful security action and rejected the rights groups' account.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said Egyptian authorities had arrested hundreds of people in the two weeks before COP27 for alleged support of peaceful protest calls, including at least 151 under Supreme State Security Prosecution investigation.
evidence.title: Egypt: Arrests over calls for protests during COP27 expose reality of human rights crisis
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said Egyptian authorities had arrested hundreds of people in the two weeks before COP27 for alleged support of peaceful protest calls, including at least 151 under Supreme State Security Prosecution investigation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous independent rights reporting with a specific detainee count and legal process details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Egyptian authorities under Sisi's control.
contrary_evidence: The government could argue the arrests were preventive security measures.

evidence.claim: The report lists credible reports of unlawful killings, enforced disappearances, torture, harsh prison conditions, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, restrictions on assembly and association, GBV, and violence targeting LGBTQI+ people, and says the government did not consistently punish abusive officials.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The report lists credible reports of unlawful killings, enforced disappearances, torture, harsh prison conditions, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, restrictions on assembly and association, GBV, and violence targeting LGBTQI+ people, and says the government did not consistently punish abusive officials.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. government country report summarizing multiple 2022 abuses and enforcement failures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level assessment under Sisi's administration, not a direct personal act.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some prosecutions of terrorist attacks and some women being appointed to judicial posts.

evidence.claim: HRW says that in 2022 Egypt continued forced disappearances, torture, flawed mass-trial practices, arbitrary travel bans and asset freezes, prison abuses, repression around COP27, and re-arrest of some released detainees.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Egypt
evidence.excerpt: HRW says that in 2022 Egypt continued forced disappearances, torture, flawed mass-trial practices, arbitrary travel bans and asset freezes, prison abuses, repression around COP27, and re-arrest of some released detainees.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: High-quality annual country chapter synthesizing 2022 reporting across detention, prison, protest, refugees, and gender/sexuality issues.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government and security institutions; some items are also structural or inherited.
contrary_evidence: HRW also notes some detainee releases and the national dialogue, but says these did not end the repression campaign.

evidence.claim: HRW documented 11 incidents of sexual violence in Egypt between 2016 and 2022 against refugees and asylum seekers and said police often refused reports or failed to investigate, leaving vulnerable women and girls without protection or justice.
evidence.title: Egypt: Sexually Abused Refugees Find No Justice
evidence.excerpt: HRW documented 11 incidents of sexual violence in Egypt between 2016 and 2022 against refugees and asylum seekers and said police often refused reports or failed to investigate, leaving vulnerable women and girls without protection or justice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed investigation with victim interviews and documentation of police failure to respond.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Egyptian police and justice authorities under Sisi; the report concerns protection failure, not private crime alone.
contrary_evidence: The report notes some aid and registration structures exist, but says they did not produce real protection or justice.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said Egypt showed no genuine will to address its human rights crisis and used the National Human Rights Strategy as a propaganda tool while continuing repression ahead of COP27.
evidence.title: Egypt: Human rights crisis deepens one year after national human rights strategy launched
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said Egypt showed no genuine will to address its human rights crisis and used the National Human Rights Strategy as a propaganda tool while continuing repression ahead of COP27.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights analysis tying official reform rhetoric to ongoing repression in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly critiques the Sisi administration's human-rights policy and messaging.
contrary_evidence: The government could argue the strategy and related initiatives signaled reform intent.

evidence.claim: The presidential pardon committee said it finalized measures to release 30 prisoners held in pre-trial detention and would keep working with prosecution and Interior to release more detainees.
evidence.title: Presidential pardon committee finalizes measures to release 30 prisoners
evidence.excerpt: The presidential pardon committee said it finalized measures to release 30 prisoners held in pre-trial detention and would keep working with prosecution and Interior to release more detainees.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official statement on a specific detainee-release action in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi-backed pardon mechanism and state prosecutorial process.
contrary_evidence: The release of 30 people is modest relative to the scale of reported arbitrary detention.

evidence.claim: Sisi publicly declared 2022 the year of civil society and urged state bodies to create a dialogue platform with local and international NGOs.
evidence.title: Sisi declares 2022 as year of civil society
evidence.excerpt: Sisi publicly declared 2022 the year of civil society and urged state bodies to create a dialogue platform with local and international NGOs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential statement, useful as favorable rhetoric and stated intent.
contrary_evidence: Rights reporting shows that the rhetoric did not prevent arrests, travel bans, and pressure on civil society during 2022.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Egypt showcased prison reforms, a five-year human rights strategy, a new rights council, and the lifting of the state of emergency, while critics called the steps superficial and said political prisoners remained detained.
evidence.title: Egypt reforms prisons and highlights rights, in moves critics call hollow
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Egypt showcased prison reforms, a five-year human rights strategy, a new rights council, and the lifting of the state of emergency, while critics called the steps superficial and said political prisoners remained detained.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting that captures both official claims and critical rebuttal.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level reform posture under Sisi, with clear limits on practical effect.
contrary_evidence: The same article quotes critics who say the reforms are cosmetic and do not improve detainee treatment.

unresolved_gaps: There is no direct 2022 ruler-attributed nuclear command, safety, or crisis decision in the file.
El Dabaa evidence is mostly permits, construction milestones, and project self-reporting, not independent safety enforcement.
The package shows mediation and diplomatic statements, but not the internal decision chain or independent proof that Egypt's mediation changed outcomes.
There is little direct evidence on any offensive military option or coercive-force decision in 2022.
The chain from abuse to personal or cabinet-level accountability is thin, especially for prisons, police, and protest repression.
The limited remedial evidence is not outcome-verified; pardons and release gestures need follow-through data.
There was no live national election in 2022, so contestability and succession are inferred largely from retrospective rights reporting.
The internal effect of dialogue initiatives and jail releases on pluralism is not independently shown.
Hard verification of State Ownership Policy implementation and actual divestments by year-end is thin.
Household-level welfare effects of inflation, transfers, and bread security are incompletely tied to ruler action.
The package lacks direct ruler-level attribution for social-welfare decisions beyond ministerial and partner-mediated actions.
There is little completed-outcome evidence for 2022 on poverty, learning loss, malnutrition, and sanitation after the interventions.
Direct evidence of personal assets, beneficial ownership, procurement gains, or family enrichment is still missing.
The file has one clear public denial and several propaganda or censorship claims, but fewer independently verified false statements with explicit contradiction.
The core 2022 economic program is reconstructed from speeches, policy papers, and partial implementation steps rather than a single explicit governing program document.
Independent verification of divestment, budget execution, and durable follow-through is still thin.
